title: Loch Ness Monster Sightings Skyrocketed In 2026, But One Scientist Thinks He Knows What's Really Going On

content:
Sightings of the Loch Ness Monster have more than doubled in 2026 compared to last year. However, one scientist who has spent years studying Nessie sightings isn’t buying into the excitement.

According to the Official Loch Ness Monster Sightings Register, 15 sightings of the legendary creature have been reported this year. That’s up from just six in all of 2025.

However, Charles Paxton, a research fellow in statistical ecology at the University of St. Andrews in Scotland, says there’s “nothing special” about the increase, telling Fox News, “The numbers fluctuate a lot year on year.”

He also pointed out, stating the obvious, that despite its name, the Official Loch Ness Monster Sightings Register isn’t actually an official scientific database.

Scientist Has A Few Explanations For All These Loch Ness Monster Sightings

Unlike many, Charles Paxton doesn’t believe a mysterious, undiscovered creature lives in Loch Ness. He also doesn’t believe the people who claim to have seen Nessie are necessarily making things up.

“I don’t think that’s the case at all,” he said.

Instead, he believes people are seeing things like animals swimming in the water, boat wakes, wind-driven waves, and floating vegetation.

“In my view, the Loch Ness Monster has lots of different sources,” Paxton explained.

Of course, that doesn’t necessarily explain every Loch Ness Monster sighting.

As Nature World News points out, a DNA study of Loch Ness found no evidence of prehistoric reptiles, but it did find plenty of eel DNA. That has led to speculation that some sightings could involve unusually large eels. Then again, in 2023, that theory seemed to be debunked, so who knows?

There Have Been Some Pretty Strange Loch Ness Monster Sightings In 2026

Back in September, we reported on a local sailor who claimed to have seen an “oversized crocodile head” sticking out of Loch Ness. That was the 15th “official” sighting reported this year.

In August, we covered three more sightings of Nessie, including one in which a witness claimed the creature’s tail sent water flying over its head. An American tourist also claimed to have seen the Loch Ness Monster while riding on a tour bus.

And in March, longtime Nessie hunter Eoin O’Faodhagain captured the first reported webcam sighting of 2026.

Paxton says the modern fascination with the Loch Ness Monster dates back to the 1930s, when sightings attracted so many tourists that traffic jams developed around the loch.

Almost 100 years later, people are still looking for Nessie. And despite what scientists think, they apparently won’t be stopping anytime soon.
